sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Lookup table for misread units
sections.what: Holds a fixed dictionary of misspelled unit strings and the correct unit each one should become, grouped by unit family.
sections.why: Likely reason: the same OCR errors repeat, so a table is a fast and predictable fix.
sections.watch_out: All keys are lowercase, so a new entry must also be lowercase or it will never match.

sections.name: PostProcessor
sections.title: Class with unit and structuring methods
sections.what: Cleans a single unit string by trimming it, swapping look-alike characters, checking the table, and then trying two pattern rules. It also picks the output shape based on the document type.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the docstrings, which describe repairing OCR misreads.
sections.watch_out: Digits are swapped for letters before the table lookup, so a legitimate unit containing a 1 would be changed.

summary: Turns the raw items found by the text-reading step into clean, typed data, and repairs common misread medical units such as mgidl into mg/dL.
purpose: Takes the extracted items and shapes them into a list of lab tests or a list of medications that the rest of the app can store and show.
why: OCR often reads the slash in a unit as the letter i, the letter l, or the digit 1. A fixed lookup table and simple pattern rules repair the most common mistakes before the data is saved.
how: First the unit text is trimmed, lowercased, and has look-alike characters swapped. That result is checked against a fixed table. If it is not in the table, two pattern rules try to rebuild the slash. Then the document type decides whether lab results or medications are collected into a list with a count.
inputs: A list of items, each with a label and a metadata dictionary, plus a document type string such as lab_report or prescription. Unit text may be empty or missing.
outputs: For lab reports, a dictionary with a tests list and a count. For prescriptions, a dictionary with a medications list and a count. Other document types return the raw items unchanged.
risks: A wrong entry in the lookup table silently changes medical units. A unit that truly contains a digit 1 would be altered. Items missing a label or metadata field raise an error instead of being skipped, which can stop the whole list.
debug: If a unit looks wrong in the app, first check the raw unit text in the OCR output. Then check the lookup table and the pattern rules in normalize_unit. Run the tests in test_normalizer to see what the function returns for the same input.
